body.objective: Students will be able to create a design concept.
body.iCan: I can create a design concept.
successCriteria: I can develop a design concept from a script
I can communicate design choices through a mood board and rendering
I can explain how design supports the director's vision
body.hook: The set of a production of "Romeo and Juliet" could be an Italian piazza, a modern city with graffiti walls, or a bare stage with two ladders. Same play, completely different meaning. Designers don't decorate a play; they interpret it.

study.title: Designing Meaning
study.question: How do designers turn a script into a visual concept?
study.passage:
Script: choose a play the class knows (for example "Antigone," "A Doll's House" or a student one-act).
Step 1, Find the core (10 minutes): Write three words that capture the play's world and feeling (for example "suffocating, polished, trapped" for "A Doll's House").
Step 2, Concept statement (10 minutes): One sentence: "This production is set in ___ to show ___." Example: "This production of 'Antigone' is set in a modern surveillance state of grey concrete and cameras to show the power of one voice against control."
Step 3, Mood board (20 minutes): Collect 10 to 15 images, colours, textures and fabric samples that match the concept.
Step 4, Rendering (20 minutes): Choose one area: set, costume or lighting. Make a rendering (sketch or digital) with labels for colours, materials and key choices.
Step 5, Pitch (5 minutes per group): Present your concept and explain how each choice connects to the play's themes.
Critic's corner: After watching a live or recorded production, write a short review: describe, analyze how design supported meaning, evaluate with evidence.
study.source: Original design task written for this lesson.

study.product: Present a design package (concept statement, mood board, labelled rendering) and write a 300-word review of a production focused on design.

examples.title: Concept statement
examples.problem: Write a concept for "Romeo and Juliet."
examples.answer: "Set in a divided modern city where gang colours mark territory, to show how inherited hatred traps young people"

examples.title: Colour palette
examples.problem: Choose a palette for a play about grief.
examples.answer: Muted greys and blues with one warm accent for memory

examples.title: Costume as character
examples.problem: How could Nora's costume change in "A Doll's House"?
examples.answer: Decorative, restrictive dress early; plain practical clothes at the end as she leaves

examples.title: Review
examples.problem: Write a review sentence analyzing lighting.
examples.answer: "Cold side lighting isolated Creon, showing his loneliness, and was one of the production's strongest choices"

practice.a: Changes in colour, fit or style show inner change.
Colours, materials and labelled key choices.

practice.q: What three things should a review do?
Why might a director update a classic's setting?
practice.a: To make themes feel urgent and connected to today.

practice.q: How can design overpower the actors?
practice.a: Busy sets, loud sound or flashy effects can distract from the story.
Evidence-based judgments about what the production aimed to do.

practice.q: How do all designers keep a production unified?
practice.a: By following the same concept and palette.
